_comment: Reads local agent state only - no network, no credentials. Empty agents discovers whatever this machine has; naming them instead fixes the set and the order and turns discovery off. exclude_agents drops one either way. A leftover section still named usage is read as this one, and the pane says so.

claude.help: What the claude subscription costs you per month - the whole plan, not a rate per token. Set it and METERED gains 'the plan saves': the month's list-price cost minus this. 0 or unset leaves that line off, because nothing on this machine knows what you pay.

_auto_detect_agent_comment: Show whatever agents this machine turns out to have. On, which is what has always happened when no set was named - it was simply spelt as an empty list, which nothing on screen could name. While it is on, agents below is ignored; exclude_agents still applies, so dropping one does not mean naming all the others. Turn it off to show exactly the agents picked, in that order. Leave the key out entirely and the old rule decides: a named list wins, an empty one discovers.
_agents_comment: Agent names to show, in the order given; empty discovers whatever local state this machine has. Pick from the list rather than typing: a name that is not one of the six is not an error, it is simply an agent that never appears.
_exclude_agents_comment: Agents to leave out, applied either way - to the ones discovered automatically and to a list named by hand. Picked from the same six, so an exclusion cannot be spelt wrongly and silently do nothing.
_refresh_comment: Seconds between local state and allowed quota refreshes.
_rates_comment: OPTIONAL override, in US$ per million tokens, keyed by model. Published list prices ship in the code, dated on screen, so Claude models are priced with no config at all. Set entries here to correct a stale price, to add a provider that publishes none (OpenAI, xAI), or to use your own negotiated rates. Each model carries the five priced kinds - input, output, cache_read, cache_write, cache_write_1h. Reasoning tokens are not among them: vendors count them inside output, so pricing them again would charge them twice. Longest matching model name wins and '*' catches the rest.
_plan_cost_comment: What each subscription costs you per month, per agent, in US$. A flat monthly figure - the per-token prices are `rates`, which is a different setting. Nothing ships here: plans vary by tier and region, and no invoice is on this machine. Set one and METERED gains 'the plan saves' - the month's cost at list prices against what you actually pay.
_antigravity_remote_comment: Antigravity publishes its quota two ways: a language server that runs inside the app, and Google, which serves the same summary on the endpoint the tier already comes from. The local one is preferred and this only decides whether the remote one may be asked when the app is shut. On by default - it is the same host and the same credential the tier request already uses. Turn it off and the quota is absent whenever Antigravity is closed; the tab then says so, and names this key.
_antigravity_start_comment: Whether the widget may start the `agy` CLI to read the quota it serves, when nothing else has one. On by default, and the only setting here that runs another program. It is your own CLI, already installed and signed in; it is started under a pseudo-terminal, killed by pid as soon as the reading is taken, and reaped, so nothing outlives the fetch; and a CLI you started yourself is found by the ordinary local probe long before this runs, so this can never shut one of yours down. Off means the quota lasts an hour past the last time Antigravity ran, which is the token's life.
_grok_ping_comment: Grok is the only agent with no live quota: its figures come from the log its own CLI writes, so they move only when you use Grok on this machine. Turn grok_ping on to ask x.ai instead, using the token the CLI leaves in ~/.grok/auth.json. That also runs the Grok CLI once after a session goes quiet, which is what refreshes the token - without it the asking works until the token lapses and then silently stops. Off by default: a widget that reads should not start talking to a vendor, or starting somebody else's program, because it was launched.
_grok_ping_minutes_comment: Minutes between enabled Grok quota polls.
